title: A Reconstruction of Proto-Tangkhulic Rhymes
alternate_titles: Diachronic Phonology and Coda Developments in Tangkhulic
subject: Historical Phonology & Sino-Tibetan Rhymes
notes: Landmark LTBA study demonstrating the regular diachronic evolution of rhymes from Proto-Tibeto-Burman to Proto-Tangkhulic.
abstract: We reconstruct the rhyme system of Proto-Tangkhulic (PTk) based on a comparative corpus of over 800 cognate sets spanning Standard Tangkhul (Ukhrul), Huishu, Kachai, Champhung, and Tusom. We demonstrate that Proto-Tangkhulic distinguished phonemic vowel length before dental and velar codas (*-a:t vs *-at; *-a:k vs *-ak), and retained the Proto-Tibeto-Burman lateral coda *-l, which merged into front glides or open vowels in Standard Tangkhul. This reconstruction resolves longstanding anomalies in the external comparison of Tangkhul with Jingpho and Lolo-Burmese.

sections.title: 1. The PTk Rhyme Inventory
sections.content: The reconstructed rhyme inventory of Proto-Tangkhulic includes 24 distinct rhymes with stop and nasal codas: *-am, *-an, *-aŋ, *-ap, *-at, *-ak, *-a:t, *-a:k, *-im, *-in, *-iŋ, *-ip, *-it, *-ik, *-um, *-un, *-uŋ, *-up, *-ut, *-uk, and lateral rhymes *-al, *-il, *-ul. While Standard Tangkhul regularly neutralizes vowel length before codas, the conservative Huishu dialect preserves qualitative differences that verify the length distinction.

tangkhul_data.notes: Reflects PTk *Cə-pi:k (long vowel before velar stop).
PTk *to:l (preservation of final lateral in Huishu).

sections.title: 2. Evolution of Lateral Codas (*-l)
sections.content: One of the major breakthroughs of Proto-Tangkhulic historical phonology is recognizing the regular fate of PTB *-l. In Standard Ukhrul, PTB *-l vocalized to a high front offglide [-i] after back vowels (e.g. *tul > tui 'speech'; *ŋul > ngui 'silver/money'). In Huishu, *-l is preserved intact as an alveolar lateral continuant [-l], proving that lateral loss in Ukhrul was a secondary innovation of the central dialect group.

tangkhul_data.notes: Direct cognate with Written Tibetan dngul.
Preservation of liquid coda in archaic peripheral varieties.

sections.title: 3. Implications for Sino-Tibetan Subgrouping
sections.content: Recognizing the conservative nature of Proto-Tangkhulic rhymes provides a crucial benchmark for the genetic classification of the Indo-Burma borderlands. Tangkhulic shares specific rhyme mergers with Maring and Kuki-Chin, yet preserves distinct prefixal morphology that establishes it as a primary coordinate branch of Tibeto-Burman.

tangkhul_data.notes: PTk *siŋ cognate with Written Burmese sac and Tibetan shing.
